criteria.name: Thumb-stop cover
criteria.notes: The raised hero ridge landed. A dark dune now crosses the frame from about y 1220 to 1600 display, and its lit flank and fine grain at lower right give the lower half a foreground-to-midground read it lacked. The cover still makes a named tension in 8 words in 163 px type, and the gold 8 is echoed by the rail notch. It holds at 8 and not 9 for three reasons: the brightest, sharpest region is the lower-right slope rather than one crest; there is no repoussoir lip; and the band from y 950 to 1100 is still empty sky with a faint teal glow. It reads as handsome night snow, not unmistakably the Coastal Plain.

criteria.name: Story arc & swipe momentum
criteria.notes: The copy is unchanged. The range (01) is paid on 02, 05's admission is the turn, 07 complicates it, and 09 closes on the same 2 to 16. Weak junctions remain: 03 to 04 never prints 12 = 10 + 2, 04 plants nothing for 05, and 08 ('IF AUTHORIZED') could move without loss.

criteria.name: Artwork craft & genuine detail
criteria.notes: The craft cycle produced real but partial gains. 01 now has a modelled ridge with depth. On 04 the hollow size and spacing jitter reduces the drilled look somewhat. 07 has larger shelves and slabs, and the dead hachure pool is gone. On 08 the side glass is now a clean dark pane instead of pixel noise. Against the renders as they stand: 08, the claimed rendered-ladder hero, is still untextured boxes. Its tracks are black lozenges with no visible road wheels, lugs or baseplate. The vermilion stripe still breaks into streaky dither from x 1080 to 1450 display at y 1335. The eleven clones are the same conga line at nearly full saturation, with no visible fog grade. The blown white smudge at lower right (x 1100 to 1600, y 1600 to 1900) remains. 05 barely moved: the aurora is still a right-side patch whose glowing base reads as a lit hill. The new far ridge is a thin silhouette, and the left half from y 1100 to 1450 is still dead. On 07, the two den-model slabs interpenetrate at x 1305 rather than abutting, the lower band from y 1600 to 1760 is an empty murky glow, and the slabs are flat-shaded cubes with no ground contact. 04 is still a perforated plate rather than pressed snow, and the band from y 650 to 880 is still empty. 02, 03 and 06 stay strong and carry the score. This is up half a point, not a full point, because the most damaging frame (08) changed least visibly.

one_sentence_fix: Slide 08 still decides the art score: give the hero vibroseis visible road wheels and lugged tread, a baseplate and mast between the tracks, and a clean solid stripe decal, and push the eleven clones into a progressive exp2 fog so the line recedes instead of marching at full saturation.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The rendered-ladder hero is still untextured boxes. The tracks are featureless black lozenges with no visible road wheels, lugs or baseplate. The vermilion stripe dithers into streaks across x 1080 to 1450, y 1335 display. The eleven clones march at near-full saturation with no visible fog. A blown white smudge fills the lower right (x 1100 to 1600, y 1600 to 1900).
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Light the track sides so road wheels and tread lugs read. Model the vibrator pad between the tracks. Render the stripe as one solid quad offset off the body, with no z-fight. Apply exp2 fog of about 0.04 so the clones fade to the sky tone. Clamp the lower-right snow to the frame's highlight ceiling.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: This is effectively unchanged. The aurora is a single right-side patch whose glowing base reads as a lit hill outline. The new far ridge is a thin dark line, the left half from y 1100 to 1450 display is still dead, and the sea plain is sparse dash ripples.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Draw faint, low rays across the full width at two further depths, so the left third carries dim curtain light. Remove the bright base edge so the curtain fades into the horizon instead of outlining a hill.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The two den-model slabs interpenetrate at x 1305 display. All slabs are flat-shaded cubes with no contact shadow on their shelves. The band from y 1600 to 1760, below the third shelf, is an empty murky glow that replaced the hachures but does no work.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Abut the den-model slabs edge to edge, with the second offset in depth, and give every slab a soft contact shadow on its shelf. Then either tighten the shelf spacing so the third shelf sits lower, or let the ground plane catch the slabs' casts across that band.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The jitter helped, but it still reads as a perforated metal plate: hard-edged elliptical holes with no softened snow rims or grain on the slab top, and an empty band from y 650 to 880 display between body and slab.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Soften each hollow's rim with a lit lip and inner shading gradient and add fine snow grain to the slab top. Raise the slab about 150 px so its far edge sits just under the body copy.

editor_notes_for_email: Re-scored after the one CRAFT FLOOR cycle: 8.62 against the round-3 threshold of 8.0, so it ships. Artwork craft rose from 7 to 7.5. That is still under the 8.5 floor, but the one cycle owed has been spent, and the floor is never a reason not to ship. The remaining art debt is mainly slide 8: the vibroseis is still blocky, with streaky stripe dither and no fog on the line. Slide 5's aurora barely changed. The rubric's weights sum to 1.10, which inflates every total by about 10 percent; normalised, this deck is 7.83, and the rubric file should be corrected in a machine pass. site_fresh must be rebuilt and committed before the merge, and the Gmail draft follows the merge. Honesty locks to keep in replies: the 2025 survey dates are only what the proposed terms list, the cap of 10 also covers bears away from dens (the den-only median is 4), and the den model is a statistical simulation in R, not AI. Comments close December 17th, so after that date slides 7 and 9 carry a stale ask. Session effort read medium, not the high the settings carry.
